transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Head DS, Nebula), Markus Lenz (CTO), Sam Carter (Platform Eng), Eva Zhou (Product)

Summary (auto): Kickoff focused on unit-economics and performance scoping. High-level agreement to run a 3-week bench sprint with 5 workload profiles and then a 3-week pilot with committed capacity if targets met.

Shared artifacts: cost-model spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/share/nebula-cost-model), bench harness repo (link: https://github.com/redwood/bench-harness), security checklist doc (short link).

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (AE): Okay everyone um thanks for joining, happy holidays, we'll try to keep this tight. Quick intros, then go into the scope — Luis will drive the bench plan.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks Maya, yeah — excited. We want to understand the per-token economics before we commit to any capacity. Our use case is customer conversation summarization and an embeddings index for retrieval. Latency matters for interactive agents.
[00:32] Markus: From infra side we care about burst and cost predictability. We'll also need audit logs for compliance.
[00:40] Luis (SE): Great. I'll outline the benchmark profiles, the knobs we'll exercise (batch size, wait-ms, kv/prefix cache), and what metrics we capture — tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, tokens/GPU-hour, and cost per 1k tokens estimated from runtime numbers.
[01:05] Eva: Quick question, when you say cost per 1k tokens do you include embedding/ index costs? We have nightly batch embedding jobs too.
[01:12] Maya: Good call. We'll separate interactive generation cost and batch embedding cost; the model variants differ. We'll give per-workload tables.

[02:10] Luis: Proposed workload profiles — five of them: 1) Interactive chat summarization (avg prompt 120 tokens, avg reply 60 tokens, target p50 < 200ms), 2) High-throughput chat (short Q/A 30->20 tokens, 200 concurrent sessions), 3) Retrieval+rerank (512 token context + rerank top50), 4) Embeddings batch (nightly 2M docs, throughput target), 5) Long-context analysis (4k context, lower qps). Each will have accuracy/quality checks — e.g., ROUGE for summarization and ranking precision for rerank.
[03:02] Priya: For interactive we care about latency under 250ms ideally; p95 can be higher but try to keep p50 tight. Cost target is to be within 2x of our current baseline (on-prem) for 90% of interactions while improving time-to-insight. In dollars, rough runway: $30K/month for the feature initial bucket.
[03:25] Maya: Noted — we'll map to per-token estimates. As a ballpark, we'll model FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants; typical delta is ~2-3x cost reduction with 4-bit at some quality regression. We'll show quality vs cost curves.

[04:10] Markus: On deployment: we prefer VPC private deployment but open to Redwood hosted if committed throughput and encryption/KMS match our compliance. Also SSO via SAML.
[04:24] Luis: We can run Private with VPC peering and KMS. For benchs we'll need sample traffic and a short-lived permissioned endpoint.

[06:00] Luis: Bench parameters we'll vary: max_batch_size (8, 32, 64), batch_wait_ms (10, 25, 50), kv cache enabled/disabled, prefix cache TTLs, and quantization modes (FP16, PTQ 4-bit, int3-ish experimental). We'll capture cold vs warm KV cache numbers to estimate amortized token cost.
[06:30] Sam: Our infra note: we have a 10Gbps link, and can't accept inbound peering without approval; we need to test via a jump host. I'll share the net constraints.

[08:45] Priya: On quality: for summarization we will run our gold set (2k examples) and measure compressive ROUGE & hallucination rate. We need hallucination under 1.5% for release.
[09:05] Luis: Good — we'll add that to bench harness. For reranking we'll compute NDCG@10 against our labeled set.

[12:30] Maya: Success criteria — let's read them out: 1) interactive p50 latency < 200ms for the small chat profile; 2) p95 < 900ms; 3) cost per 1k tokens <= $0.35 in target config OR 2x improvement over baseline; 4) hallucination < 1.5% on gold prompts; 5) embeddings throughput meets nightly window (2M docs in <6 hours) — does that sound right?
[12:58] Priya: Yup that's reasonable. The $0.35/1k tokens is a soft number — we want to see tradeoffs.
[13:20] Markus: If we can get committed capacity discounts that's attractive. We'll consider a 12-month contract if numbers look good.

[15:10] Luis: Benchmark timeline: week 0 (this week) gather samples & prework, week 1-3 bench sprint — run 3 quant configs across 5 profiles, compile cost model; week 4-6 pilot with limited production traffic and monitoring plus final econ review.
[15:38] Eva: Can we get a shorter proof, like a two-week rapid sanity, before committing to full bench?
[15:45] Maya: We can do a 1-week smoke bench to validate assumptions — run a small sample to choose configs, then full 3-week bench. So: 1-week smoke -> 3-week bench -> pilot.

[18:00] Luis: Cost modeling approach: take tokens/sec from runtime, compute tokens per GPU-hour, then multiply by GPU-hour price plus amortized infra (storage, networking), then add per-request overheads. We'll produce a per-1k-token table for each profile and config. We'll also show sensitivity to batch_wait_ms and concurrency.
[18:30] Priya: Important — show the savings from prefix/KV cache. Many of our chats re-use context. If caching drops token generation by 20% that's huge.
[18:45] Luis: Yep, we'll capture cold vs warm percentages. We'll also show a recommended batching policy: e.g., dynamic batching up to 40 with 25ms wait threshold for interactive, and dedicated large batches for embeddings.

[22:10] Sam: Observability: we need per-route token/latency/cost breakdown in the console and audit logs shipped to our SIEM.
[22:25] Maya: Redwood Console supports token-level cost at route granularity; we'll demo the dashboard during bench walkthrough. Audit logs can ship to your S3 or SIEM via syslog connector — we'll add the config to the security doc.

[25:00] Priya: A question on accuracy vs quant: do you have examples where 4-bit PTQ breaks summarization fidelity?
[25:10] Luis: It depends on model family. Some transformer families tolerate PTQ well; others need quant-aware fine-tune. We'll run evaluation and flag any ROUGE drops >3 points. If that happens we'll include a hybrid policy: host-critical flows on FP16 or lowered quant while background tasks use quant.

[28:40] Markus: For pricing we need scenarios: fully hosted on-demand, 6/12 month reserved compute, and private deployment licensing. Provide delta sheet.
[28:56] Maya: We'll include hosted on-demand, 6-month reserved commit, and an example private licensing stack with support costs. We'll show effective $/1k tokens at each commit tier.

[32:10] Luis: Bench infra note: we'll run on the smallest GPU instance that still meets latency SLO for interactive; then scale to larger instances for throughput tests. We'll capture tokens/GPU-hour. Also run an SLO violation sensitivity test: spike to 3x qps for 2 mins.
[33:05] Priya: Good, we need to see graceful degradation: fall back to smaller cheaper models or queueing policy.
[33:20] Luis: We'll simulate fallbacks: route to smaller model variants or cached summary if available. We'll measure user-perceived latency.

[36:00] Eva: Timeline/decision criteria — if bench shows p50 target and cost <= target, we proceed with a 6-week pilot and then decide on commit. If not, we'll iterate on prompt engineering and caching.
[36:15] Maya: Exactly. We'll aim to have bench results and cost model by Jan 13 so you can make a decision in the following week.

[40:12] Markus: Security items: SOC2, KMS integration, RBAC, and audit retention. We'll need a short security review next week.
[40:25] Maya: I'll attach the SOC2 cert and the KMS integration playbook. We can schedule a 45m call with security folks if needed.

[43:00] Luis: Practical knobs we'll try in bench: 1) max_batch_size ramp 8->64, 2) batch_wait_ms 5->50ms, 3) token-level KV cache TTL 10m->24h, 4) dynamic routing by latency budget. For each experiment we'll log: throughput, per-token CPU/GPU breakdown, mem usage, and latency histogram.
[45:30] Priya: For embeddings we want a projected cost per million embeddings at FP16 and 8-bit quantized. Also index build time for our nightly window.
[45:44] Luis: We'll include those two numbers. Expect big gains with 8-bit packed matrix multiply for embedding-only runs.

[49:10] Sam: On network: we might enforce egress limits. If benchmarks show heavy egress we'll need to re-architect. I'll supply network constraints.
[49:25] Maya: Noted. We'll annotate cost model with bandwidth sensitivity.

[52:00] Priya: Anything else?
[52:05] Eva: One more — show dashboard alerting thresholds for hallucination and degredation. We want automatic rollback to a safe model.
[52:18] Luis: We'll include an alerting config: rolling eval on a canary set, if hallucination > 2% over baseline then auto-fallback to safer model.
[52:35] Maya: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Luis runs benchmarks and posts logs, Maya sends pricing and security artifacts, customer sends sample prompts and infra constraints. We'll tentatively meet for bench walkthrough the week of Jan 10.
[53:00] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[53:05] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the calendar and links.
[56:30] (call ends)
